issue.title: sase validate and sase init memory --check disagree about sase/memory/sase_sizes.md, so running the mandatory memory init flips just check red
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-mq.3 (epic sase-mq, Enforce user-owned primary workspace boundaries) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-16T06:16:10Z, and independently reproduced by sase-mq's landing agent at HEAD ec390cdd4 in workspace sase_16 on a clean tree.

ROOT CAUSE (precise): the two entry points that check generated memory drift resolve different template sources for the same generated note, so they give opposite answers for the same file at the same commit.

REPRODUCTION (clean worktree, HEAD ec390cdd4, after just install):

  $ .venv/bin/sase validate
  SASE validation
    ok     init memory --check      <-- GREEN
    ok     init repo --check
    ok     init skills --check
    ok     plan links validate
    ok     agent prompts validate

  $ sase init memory --check --diff
  Needs attention:
    run  init memory  update 2 memory files and provider shims
         ~ update  sase/memory/sase_sizes.md  +5 -4  generated SASE size memory
         ~ update  sase/memory/README.md      +4 -4  memory README

The planned sase_sizes.md rewrite changes the alias wording in both directions of the note:

  -`medium`, `large`, `xlarge`. Size chooses the default work model through the matching
  -`@<size>` built-in alias and decides whether the worker plans before implementing. An
  +`medium`, `large`, `xlarge`. Size chooses the default work model through
  +`@<size>_worker` aliases and decides whether the worker plans before implementing. An

  -Default model aliases are `@xsmall`, `@small`, `@medium`, `@large`, and `@xlarge`. An
  -explicit `model` on a bead or plan takes precedence.
  +Default model aliases are `@xsmall_worker`, `@small_worker`, `@medium_worker`,
  +`@large_worker`, and `@xlarge_worker`. An explicit `model` on a bead or plan takes
  +precedence.

plus a mechanical line/token-count refresh in sase/memory/README.md.

WHY IT MATTERS: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md make 'sase memory init' mandatory after any memory file edit. Following that mandated workflow rewrites sase_sizes.md to the `@<size>_worker` wording, which is what 'just check' then has to accept -- but 'just check' runs 'sase validate', whose 'init memory --check' step is green only on the committed `@<size>` wording. So the required post-edit step is exactly what turns the gate red, and the agent is left choosing between an unrelated 2-file diff in their commit and a red check. Phase sase-mq.3 worked around it by deliberately leaving generated memory at HEAD so validate stayed green, which means the drift is still latent for the next agent.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS UNRESOLVED: grep finds no `_worker` alias anywhere in this repo (src/sase/default_config.yml, src/sase/xprompts/), so the `@<size>_worker` wording appears to come from the home/global (chezmoi) memory template rather than the project template. Determining the authoritative alias names is part of this task; do not assume the generator is right.

SCOPE: reconcile the two check paths so 'sase validate' and 'sase init memory --check' agree on a single template source for a project-scoped generated note, then make the committed sase/memory/sase_sizes.md match whichever alias vocabulary actually exists. Open the chezmoi repo through /sase_repo (never by guessing a path) to inspect the home/global template. Add a regression gate so a project note whose generator output differs from the committed file cannot pass 'sase validate'.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-l0 — closed task 'sase memory init --no-commit still commits generated chezmoi home instruction files'. Same home-template-vs-project-scope boundary inside sase memory init; its fix touched which files the write path treats as home/global versus project, which is the boundary this drift falls out of.

RELATED: sase-j1 — closed task 'The /sase_plan skill still classifies plan authoring as large/xlarge work after that guidance was deleted from the sizes memory'. Prior instance of consumers drifting from sase/memory/sase_sizes.md content; that task fixed a consumer, this one fixes the generator/checker disagreement that lets the note drift in the first place.

TRIAGE 2026-08-16 (workspace sase_13, master 630f4ea71, after just install). Verified fixed on a clean tree: '.venv/bin/sase validate' reports 'ok init memory --check' plus ok for init repo/init skills/plan links/agent prompts, and 'sase init memory --check --diff' independently reports 'SASE is initialized. No init subcommands need to run. Checked: memory.' -- no pending update for sase/memory/sase_sizes.md or any other generated note. The two entry points no longer disagree, so running the mandatory memory init no longer flips just check red.

payload.close_reason: No longer reproduces; sase validate and sase init memory --check now agree and both are green.

evidence.note: Independent post-close reproduction on 2026-08-16 while verifying unrelated Config Center atomic-save deflake work. After focused Config Center tests and a 10-repeat contention soak passed, just check failed only at SASE validation: .venv/bin/sase validate reports init memory --check wants ~/.local/share/chezmoi/home/sase/memory/README.md regenerated (+3/-2) to add sase_flags.md feature-flag guidance. The global sase init memory --check --diff disagrees on the same tree, wanting to remove the Feature Flags section from this project's generated sase/memory/sase.md and provider shims. No memory files were regenerated because this task did not carry owner approval for memory-file edits.

payload.entry: OBSERVATION (sase-ns.6 land agent, 2026-08-17, workspace sase_14 at HEAD 6000a54a1, clean tree after just install): 'sase init memory --check' now exits 0 with 'SASE is initialized. No init subcommands need to run.', and 'just check''s SASE validation step passes. The drift that phase sase-ns.6.2's +1 recorded is not reproducing at this HEAD. Recording as an observation rather than a close because I did not identify which commit resolved it and cannot rule out that the two entry points still disagree under a different memory-file state; the reported defect is a disagreement between 'sase validate' and 'sase init memory --check', and one green run of one of them does not prove they now agree in general.
